framework.summary: A developer must produce, follow and publish a safety and security protocol, and publish any material change within 30 days.
framework.quote: A developer shall produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol.

transparency_report.summary: A developer must publish a risk assessment report at least every 90 days.
transparency_report.quote: No less than every 90 days, a developer shall produce and conspicuously publish a risk assessment report.

incident_reporting.summary: The protocol must state when and to whom the developer will report incidents; the bill sets no reporting window or government recipient.
incident_reporting.quote: the conditions under which the developer will report incidents relevant to critical risk that have occurred in connection with one or more of its foundation models

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: At least once a year a developer must hire a reputable third-party auditor to assess its compliance with its protocol, and publish the report within 90 days.
third_party_audit.quote: At least once every calendar year, a developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report assessing the following

whistleblower.summary: The Whistleblower Act applies to employees who tell the Attorney General about critical risk, and developers must offer an anonymous internal reporting process.
whistleblower.quote: A developer shall provide a reasonable internal process through which an employee may anonymously disclose information to the developer

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A developer is covered by compute cost, not operation count: training a model with computing power costing at least $100,000,000.
compute_threshold.quote: has trained at least one foundation model with a quantity of computational power that costs at least $100,000,000

revenue_threshold.summary: A developer is covered by spending: it has trained a model with computing power costing at least $100,000,000; no revenue or user test.
revenue_threshold.quote: has trained at least one foundation model with a quantity of computational power that costs at least $100,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Critical risk means a foreseeable risk of death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage.
harm_threshold.quote: will result in the death of, or serious injury to, more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to rights in money or property

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for violating Sec. 15 or 25, and seek injunctive or declaratory relief.
penalties.quote: may be assessed a civil penalty not to exceed $1,000,000

effective_date.summary: The bill text states no effective date.

notes: Text has gaps (Sec. 35(a) lists 'Sections or 25', Sec. 25 refers to 'Section 20.5', Sec. 30(c) has a missing number of years). The summary says the Sec. 15 and 25 are the penalized sections as the following sentence reads. Compute and revenue both rest on the same cost-of-compute definition; owner may prefer compute=partial, revenue=not_in_bill.
